hints: Identify the parameters: weights are normally distributed with $\mu = 1.04$ kg and $\sigma = 0.017$ kg.
Use symmetry: $\mathrm{P}(Z < -z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$, then look up $\Phi(2.353)$ in the normal distribution table.
walkthrough: Define the normal random variable for packet weight $X \sim \mathrm{N}(1.04, 0.017^2)$:

Convert to the upper tail of the standard normal distribution:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1) = \mathrm{P}(Z < -2.353) = 1 - \Phi(2.353)$$

Look up $\Phi(2.353)$ in the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(2.353) = 0.9907$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1) = 1 - 0.9907 = 0.0093$$
teacher_walkthrough: Let $X$ denote the weight in kilograms of a packet of rice: $X \sim \mathrm{N}(1.04, 0.017^2)$. Here $\mu = 1.04\text{ kg}$ and $\sigma = 0.017\text{ kg}$.
We need to find the probability that a packet weighs less than 1 kg: $\mathrm{P}(X < 1)$.

Use the standardisation formula $Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$:
$$Z = \frac{1 - 1.04}{0.017}$$
Subtract in the numerator:
$$1 - 1.04 = -0.04$$
Divide by $0.017$:
$$Z = \frac{-0.04}{0.017} \approx -2.35294 \approx -2.353$$

Using the symmetry of the standard normal curve, the lower tail probability for a negative $Z$-score equals the complement of the cumulative probability at positive $Z$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z < -2.353) = 1 - \Phi(2.353)$$

Look up $2.353$ in the normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(2.35) = 0.9906, \quad \text{difference for } 3 \text{ is } 1 \implies \Phi(2.353) = 0.9907$$
Subtract:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1) = 1 - 0.9907 = 0.0093$$

hints: Each packet has an average weight equal to the mean: $\mu = 1.04$ kg.
Divide the total mass of 1000 kg by the average weight per packet: $\dfrac{1000}{1.04}$.
State the resulting expected number of packets as an integer or to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Use the mean weight per packet $\mu = 1.04\text{ kg}$ to find the expected number of packets filled from $1000\text{ kg}$:
$$\text{Expected packets} = \dfrac{1000}{1.04}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
On average, each packet of rice filled by the machine contains the mean amount of rice:
$$\text{Mean weight per packet} = 1.04\text{ kg}$$

Given a bulk total of $1000\text{ kg}$ of rice, find how many packets this can fill on average by dividing total mass by the average mass per packet:
$$\text{Expected number of packets} = \frac{1000}{1.04}$$

Compute the division:
$$\frac{1000}{1.04} = \frac{100000}{104} = \frac{12500}{13} \approx 961.538$$
Depending on rounding, the machine fills approximately $961$ or $962$ packets.

hints: Since $0.039 < 0.5$, the $z$-score is negative. Find $z$ using $1 - \Phi(|z|) = 0.039 \implies \Phi(|z|) = 0.961$.
Look up $0.961$ in the normal distribution table to find $|z| = 1.765$, so $z = -1.765$.
Set up the standardisation equation $\dfrac{1 - \mu}{0.017} = -1.765$ and solve for $\mu$.
walkthrough:
Set up the probability equation for the adjusted machine with mean $\mu$ and $\sigma = 0.017$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1) = 0.039$$

Find the critical $z$-value using symmetry:
$$\Phi(-z) = 0.039 \implies \Phi(|z|) = 1 - 0.039 = 0.961$$
$$|z| = 1.765 \implies z = -1.765$$
teacher_walkthrough: The machine has been adjusted to have a new mean $\mu$ while keeping the standard deviation $\sigma = 0.017\text{ kg}$: $X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, 0.017^2)$.

We are told that $3.9\%$ of packets now weigh less than 1 kg:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 1) = 0.039$$

Because $0.039 < 0.5$, the cutoff $1\text{ kg}$ lies below the mean, meaning its standard score $z$ is negative. Use the complement relation:
$$\Phi(|z|) = 1 - 0.039 = 0.961$$

Look up $0.961$ in the standard normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(1.76) = 0.9608, \quad \text{difference for } 2 \text{ is } 2 \implies \Phi(1.762) = 0.9610$$
Using inverse lookup gives $|z| \approx 1.762$ to $1.765$. Using $z = -1.765$:

Set up the standardisation formula:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \implies -1.765 = \frac{1 - \mu}{0.017}$$

Multiply both sides by $0.017$:
$$1 - \mu = -1.765 \times 0.017 = -0.030005$$

Add $\mu$ to both sides and add $0.030005$:
$$\mu = 1 + 0.030005 = 1.030005\text{ kg}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\mu = 1.03\text{ kg}$.

hints: Use the new mean weight per packet from part (iii): $\mu = 1.03$ kg.
Divide the total mass of 1000 kg by the new mean weight: $\dfrac{1000}{1.03}$.
State the resulting expected number of packets.
walkthrough:
Use the adjusted mean weight $\mu = 1.03\text{ kg}$ to calculate the new expected number of packets:
$$\text{Expected packets} = \dfrac{1000}{1.03}$$
teacher_walkthrough: With the new adjustment, each packet contains an average weight of $\mu = 1.03\text{ kg}$.

To find how many packets can be filled from $1000\text{ kg}$ of rice, divide the total mass by the new mean weight per packet:
$$\text{Expected packets} = \frac{1000}{1.03}$$

Calculate the quotient:
$$\frac{1000}{1.03} = \frac{100000}{103} \approx 970.874$$
Rounding appropriately gives an expected count of $970$ or $971$ packets.
